what: When the top edge of the photo frame touches the bottom of the screen, a circle (clip-path) opens from the top right corner to 150% in 1.6s expo.inOut, and the photo inside shrinks into place from 1.15x in 1.8s expo.out. If it is already scrolling down faster than 900px per second at 125% below the screen, it opens one step early and runs faster at speed/600 times (1~4x) — so no empty frame is left even on a fast scroll. Once only

options.at: Where the circle opens (clip-path coordinates), default ‹100% 0%› (top right) — for pages read right to left use ‹0% 0%›
options.zoom: Starting size of the inner photo as it shrinks, default 1.15 — at 1 the photo stays as is
options.early: Position it opens first on a fast scroll down, default ‹top 125%›
options.boost: Fast-spinning drain = Speed ÷ this value, default 600
options.[data-fx-part=img]: Photo (child) that shrinks — first child if none

note: Used together with a photo cell that has only one rounded corner (border-start-end-radius), the circle spreads from the rounded side so the cell shape and the motion match

from.where: shared.js reveal() — original [data-reveal]: circle(0→150% at 100% 0) 1.6s expo.inOut + img scale 1.15→1 1.8s expo.out, and if speed is 900 or more at top 125% it starts first, timeScale clamp(1,4,v/600)
